summary: The migrated WinUI 3 app faithfully replicates and exceeds the original UWP app on this machine. No functional discrepancies found in the migrated app; the only notable finding is on the UWP side (it never rendered its scenario UI).
uwp_baseline_caveat: The original UWP app launched (uwp-app-runner ok:true, process alive, window present) but remained stuck on its extended splash screen ('Windows platform sample') indefinitely; its content pane was empty in the UIA tree at depth 8 and never rendered the scenario UI. The golden screenshot is therefore splash-only, so no live UWP functional/visual reference exists for pixel comparison. This is a UWP-side environment issue (likely native OpenCVBridge/.NET Native startup), not a WinUI migration defect.

discrepancies.detail: Live camera preview, processed output, and FPS could not be exercised because no camera device is present on this machine. This gate affects both apps equally. The WinUI app correctly shows a defensive fallback: 'This sample requires a camera device that is not available on this machine.' The original UWP app returns silently on no-camera (no fallback), so the WinUI behavior is a strict improvement.
discrepancies.winui_behavior: Graceful fallback panel shown; PreviewGrid hidden.

discrepancies.detail: ComboBox present in UIA (AutomationId OperationComboBox), populated with all 5 operations (Blur, HoughLines, Contours, Histogram, MotionDetector). Manually actuated: selecting 'Contours' updated the selection and rewrote CurrentOperationTextBlock to 'Current: Contours'. Control is behaviorally alive, matching the source SelectionChanged handler.
